m.mangala.sh1: One should meditate on Viṣṇu, clad in white, bright as the moon, four-armed, with a gracious face, for the calming of all obstacles.
m.mangala.sh2: He whose attendants, the elephant-faced one and the rest, more than a hundred of them, constantly destroy obstacles — I take refuge in him, Viṣvaksena.
m.mangala.sh3: I bow to Vyāsa, the great-grandson of Vasiṣṭha, the grandson of Śakti, the stainless one, the son of Parāśara, the father of Śuka, a treasury of austerity.
m.mangala.sh4: Salutation to Vyāsa, who is Viṣṇu in form, and to Viṣṇu, who has the form of Vyāsa. Salutation indeed to the treasury of Brahman (the Veda), the descendant of Vasiṣṭha; salutation, again and again.
m.mangala.sh5: To him who is changeless, pure, eternal, the Supreme Self, whose form is ever one and the same, to Viṣṇu, the conqueror of all —
m.mangala.sh6: to him by the mere remembrance of whom one is set free from the bondage of birth and worldly existence, to Viṣṇu, the mighty Lord: salutation.
m.mangala.mantra: Om. Salutation to Viṣṇu, the mighty Lord.
m.purva.sh7: Śrī Vaiśampāyana said: Having heard the dharmas in full, and all that purifies, Yudhiṣṭhira spoke again to Bhīṣma, the son of Śantanu.
m.purva.sh8: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Who is the one God in the world? Or what is the one supreme refuge? Praising whom, and worshipping whom, may men attain the good?
m.purva.sh9: Of all dharmas, which do you hold to be the highest? By reciting what is a creature freed from the bondage of birth and worldly existence?
m.purva.sh10: Bhīṣma said: A man who praises the Lord of the world, the God of gods, the endless, the Supreme Person, with the thousand names, ever intent upon it —
m.purva.sh11: and who ever worships that imperishable Person with devotion, meditating on him, praising him, bowing to him, and offering worship to him alone —
m.purva.sh12: praising ever Viṣṇu, who has no beginning and no end, the great Lord of all the worlds, the overseer of the worlds, passes beyond all sorrow.
m.purva.sh13: — praising him who is the friend of the brāhmaṇas and the Veda, the knower of every dharma, who increases the fame of the worlds, the lord of the worlds, the great being, the source from which all beings come into being.
m.purva.sh14: This, in my view, is the greatest of all dharmas: that a man should always worship the lotus-eyed Lord with devotion, with hymns of praise.
m.purva.sh15: He who is the supreme, great radiance, he who is the supreme, great austerity, he who is the supreme, great Brahman, he who is the supreme refuge,
m.purva.sh16: he who is the purest of the pure and the most auspicious of all that is auspicious, the god of the gods, and the imperishable father of beings,
m.purva.sh17: from whom all beings come into being at the coming of the first age, and in whom they pass again into dissolution at the end of the age —
m.purva.sh18: of him, the foremost in the world, the Lord of the universe, Viṣṇu, hear from me, O King, the thousand names, which take away sin and fear.
m.purva.sh19: The names of the great-souled one that are drawn from his qualities, that are well known and have been sung by the seers, I shall tell for welfare.
m.purva.sh20: The seer of the thousand names is Vedavyāsa, the great sage; the metre is anuṣṭubh; and the deity is the Lord, the son of Devakī.
m.purva.sh21: The source of the moon (Amṛtāṃśūdbhava) is the seed, the son of Devakī (Devakīnandana) the power, and he who is praised in three Sāmans (Trisāmā) its heart; it is applied in recitation for peace.
m.purva.sh22: I bow to the all-pervading (Viṣṇu), the victorious (Jiṣṇu), the great Viṣṇu (Mahāviṣṇu), the mighty (Prabhaviṣṇu), the great Lord (Maheśvara), who takes many forms and ends the daityas, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama).
m.viniyoga: Śrī Vedavyāsa said: Om. Of this great mantra, the hymn of the divine thousand names of Śrī Viṣṇu, the seer is the Lord Śrī Vedavyāsa; the metre is anuṣṭubh; and the deity is Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, the Supreme Self, Śrīman Nārāyaṇa. The source of the moon (Amṛtāṃśūdbhava) and the radiant one (Bhānu) are the seed; the son of Devakī (Devakīnandana) and the creator (Sraṣṭā), the power; the origin of all (Udbhava), he who stirs nature into creation (Kṣobhaṇa) and the shining god (Deva), the supreme mantra; the bearer of the conch (Śaṅkhabhṛt), the holder of the sword Nandaka (Nandakī) and the bearer of the discus (Cakrī), the kīlaka (the pin that holds the mantra fast); he whose bow is Śārṅga (Śārṅgadhanvā) and the bearer of the mace (Gadādhara), the weapon; he who holds the discus in his hand (Rathāṅgapāṇi) and the imperturbable (Akṣobhya), the eye; he who is praised in three Sāmans (Trisāmā), the singer of the Sāman (Sāmaga) and the Sāman itself (Sāma), the armour; bliss (Ānanda) and the supreme Brahman (Parabrahma), the source; the season (Ṛtu), he of auspicious sight (Sudarśana) and time (Kāla), the binding of the quarters. The Lord in his universal form (Śrī Viśvarūpa) is the meditation. For the pleasure of Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, it is applied in the recitation of the thousand names.
m.nyasa.rishyadi: Om. On the head: salutation to the sage Vedavyāsa. On the mouth: salutation to the anuṣṭubh metre. In the heart: salutation to the deity, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Self. On the private parts: salutation to the seed, “amṛtāṃśūdbhavo bhānuḥ”. On the feet: salutation to the power, “devakīnandanaḥ sraṣṭā”. On the whole body: salutation to the kīlaka, “śaṅkhabhṛn nandakī cakrī”. In the hollow of the joined hands: salutation to the viniyoga, in my japa for the pleasure of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
m.nyasa.kara: Om. With “viśvaṃ viṣṇur vaṣaṭkāraḥ” (the all, the all-pervading, he for whom the call vaṣaṭ is made): salutation to the two thumbs. With “amṛtāṃśūdbhavo bhānuḥ”: salutation to the two forefingers. With “brahmaṇyo brahmakṛd brahma” (the friend of the brāhmaṇas and the Veda, the maker of Brahman, Brahman): salutation to the two middle fingers. With “suvarṇabindur akṣobhyaḥ” (golden of limb, the imperturbable): salutation to the two ring fingers. With “nimiṣo ’nimiṣaḥ sragvī” (whose eyes are closed, the unwinking, the garlanded): salutation to the two little fingers. With “rathāṅgapāṇir akṣobhyaḥ”: salutation to the palms and the backs of the hands.
m.nyasa.anga: Om. With “viśvaṃ viṣṇur vaṣaṭkāraḥ”: to the heart, salutation. With “amṛtāṃśūdbhavo bhānuḥ”: to the head, svāhā. With “brahmaṇyo brahmakṛd brahma”: to the tuft of hair on the crown, vaṣaṭ. With “suvarṇabindur akṣobhyaḥ”: to the armour, hum. With “nimiṣo ’nimiṣaḥ sragvī”: to the three eyes, vauṣaṭ. With “rathāṅgapāṇir akṣobhyaḥ”: to the weapon, phaṭ.
m.sankalpa: For the pleasure of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, I shall perform the japa of the divine thousand names of Viṣṇu: this is the resolve.
m.dhyana.dh1: In the region of the ocean of milk, on a sandy shore shining with pure gems, seated on a seat made of strings of pearls, his limbs adorned with pearls like crystal, delighted by the white, abundant clouds spread above him that pour showers of nectar, holding the discus, lotus, mace and conch in his hands — may Mukunda purify us.
m.dhyana.dh2: He whose feet are the earth, whose navel is the sky, whose breath is the wind, whose eyes are the moon and the sun, whose ears are the quarters, whose head is heaven, whose mouth is fire and whose abdomen is the ocean; within whom the universe, with gods, men, birds, cattle, serpents, gandharvas and daityas, sports on in its wonderful variety — I bow to him, Viṣṇu the Lord, whose body is the three worlds.
m.dhyana.mantra: Om. Salutation to the Lord Vāsudeva.
m.dhyana.dh3: Om. Peaceful of form, resting on the serpent, lotus-navelled, lord of the gods, the support of the universe, like the sky, with the colour of a rain cloud, beautiful of limb, the beloved of Lakṣmī, lotus-eyed, reached by yogis in meditation — I bow to Viṣṇu, who takes away the fear of worldly existence, the one Lord of all the worlds.
m.dhyana.dh4: Dark as a rain cloud, clothed in yellow silk, bearing the mark of the Śrīvatsa, his body made bright by the Kaustubha gem, full of holiness, with long eyes like lotuses — I bow to Viṣṇu, the one Lord of all the worlds.
m.dhyana.dh5: Salutation to him who is the origin of all beings, the upholder of the earth, whose forms are many, to Viṣṇu, the mighty Lord.
m.dhyana.dh6: With conch and discus, with crown and earrings, in yellow garments, lotus-eyed, with the necklace and the splendour of the Kaustubha on his chest — I bow my head to Viṣṇu, the four-armed.
m.dhyana.dh7: In the shade of the pārijāta tree, seated upon a golden throne, dark as a rain cloud, long-eyed, adorned, moon-faced, four-armed, his chest marked with the Śrīvatsa, with Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā beside him — I take refuge in Kṛṣṇa.
m.stotra.harih: Hari (the Lord who takes away sin), Om.
m.stotra.sh1: He is the universe (Viśva), the all-pervading (Viṣṇu), the one invoked with the sacrificial call vaṣaṭ (Vaṣaṭkāra), the Lord of past, future and present (Bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhu), the maker of beings (Bhūtakṛt), their sustainer (Bhūtabhṛt), pure being (Bhāva), the Self of all beings (Bhūtātmā) and the one who brings beings forth and nurtures them (Bhūtabhāvana).
m.stotra.sh2: He is the pure Self (Pūtātmā), the Supreme Self (Paramātmā) and the highest goal of the liberated (Muktānāṃ Paramā Gatiḥ); he is also the imperishable (Avyaya), the Supreme Person (Puruṣa), the witness (Sākṣī), the knower of the field, the body (Kṣetrajña), and the undecaying (Akṣara).
m.stotra.sh3: He is the one reached through yoga (Yoga), the leader of those who know yoga (Yogavidāṃ Netā), the Lord of primal nature and of the souls (Pradhānapuruṣeśvara), he whose form is the man-lion (Nārasiṃhavapu), the glorious (Śrīmān), he of beautiful hair (Keśava) and the highest of persons (Puruṣottama).
m.stotra.sh4: He is the all (Sarva), the destroyer at the dissolution (Śarva), the auspicious (Śiva), the steadfast (Sthāṇu), the source of beings (Bhūtādi) and the imperishable treasure (Nidhir Avyayaḥ); he who comes into being of his own will (Sambhava), the giver of fruits (Bhāvana), the sustainer (Bhartā), the source of all (Prabhava), the mighty (Prabhu) and the sovereign Lord (Īśvara).
m.stotra.sh5: He is the self-existent (Svayambhū), the giver of happiness (Śambhu), the sun (Āditya), the lotus-eyed (Puṣkarākṣa) and he of the mighty sound (Mahāsvana); he is without beginning or end (Anādinidhana), the supporter of all (Dhātā), the ordainer of the fruits of action (Vidhātā) and the supreme ground of all (Dhātur Uttamaḥ).
m.stotra.sh6: He is the immeasurable (Aprameya), the lord of the senses (Hṛṣīkeśa), he from whose navel springs the lotus (Padmanābha) and the lord of the immortals (Amaraprabhu); the maker of the universe (Viśvakarmā), the thinker (Manu), the fashioner of forms (Tvaṣṭā), the most vast (Sthaviṣṭha), and the ancient, the unchanging (Sthaviro Dhruvaḥ).
m.stotra.sh7: He is the one the senses cannot grasp (Agrāhya), the eternal (Śāśvata), the dark one (Kṛṣṇa), the red-eyed (Lohitākṣa) and the destroyer at the dissolution (Pratardana); he who abounds in greatness (Prabhūta), the abode of the three regions, above, below and between (Trikakubdhāma), the purifier (Pavitra) and the supreme auspiciousness (Maṅgalaṃ Param).
m.stotra.sh8: He is the ruler (Īśāna), the giver of life (Prāṇada), life itself (Prāṇa), the eldest (Jyeṣṭha), the best (Śreṣṭha) and the lord of creatures (Prajāpati); the golden womb (Hiraṇyagarbha), he who holds the earth within him (Bhūgarbha), the consort of Lakṣmī (Mādhava) and the slayer of the demon Madhu (Madhusūdana).
m.stotra.sh9: He is the almighty Lord (Īśvara), the valiant (Vikramī), the bowman (Dhanvī), the wise (Medhāvī), he who strode across the worlds (Vikrama) and he who makes all move forward (Krama); the unsurpassed (Anuttama), the unassailable (Durādharṣa), he who knows what all have done (Kṛtajña), action itself (Kṛti) and he who is established in his own Self (Ātmavān).
m.stotra.sh10: He is the lord of the gods (Sureśa), the refuge (Śaraṇa), supreme bliss (Śarma), the seed of the universe (Viśvaretā) and he from whom creatures arise (Prajābhava); he is the luminous day (Ahaḥ), the year, time itself (Saṃvatsara), he who like a serpent cannot be seized (Vyāla), knowledge itself (Pratyaya) and the all-seeing (Sarvadarśana).
m.stotra.sh11: He is the unborn (Aja), the Lord of all (Sarveśvara), the ever perfect (Siddha), fulfilment, the fruit of all (Siddhi), the origin of all (Sarvādi) and he who never falls from his nature (Acyuta); he is dharma and the boar (Vṛṣākapi), he whose nature is beyond measure (Ameyātmā) and he who stands apart from every bond (Sarvayogaviniḥsṛta).
m.stotra.sh12: He is the one who dwells in all (Vasu), he of noble mind (Vasumanā), the truth (Satya), the same Self in all (Samātmā), the unmeasured (Asammita) and the ever same (Sama); he whose worship is never in vain (Amogha), the lotus-eyed (Puṇḍarīkākṣa), he whose deeds are dharma (Vṛṣakarmā) and he whose form is dharma (Vṛṣākṛti).
m.stotra.sh13: He is the one who makes all weep at the dissolution (Rudra), the many-headed (Bahuśirā), the bearer of the worlds (Babhru), the source of the universe (Viśvayoni) and he whose fame is pure (Śuciśravā); the immortal (Amṛta), the eternal and steadfast (Śāśvatasthāṇu), the highest ascent, reaching whom none returns (Varāroha), and he of great tapas (Mahātapā).
m.stotra.sh14: He is the all-pervading (Sarvaga), the all-knowing (Sarvavit), the shining (Bhānu), he before whom hostile armies scatter everywhere (Viṣvaksena) and he who chastises the wicked (Janārdana); he is the Veda itself (Veda), the knower of the Veda (Vedavit), the flawless, complete in every part (Avyaṅga), he whose limbs are the Vedas (Vedāṅga), he who ponders the Veda (Vedavit) and the seer (Kavi).
m.stotra.sh15: He is the overseer of the worlds (Lokādhyakṣa), the overseer of the gods (Surādhyakṣa), the overseer of dharma (Dharmādhyakṣa) and both effect and cause (Kṛtākṛta); he of fourfold form (Caturātmā), of four emanations (Caturvyūha), four-tusked (Caturdaṃṣṭra) and four-armed (Caturbhuja).
m.stotra.sh16: He is the resplendent (Bhrājiṣṇu), that which is enjoyed (Bhojana), the enjoyer (Bhoktā), he who bears and overcomes all (Sahiṣṇu) and he who was born at the beginning of the world (Jagadādija); the sinless (Anagha), victory itself (Vijaya), the conqueror (Jetā), the source of the universe (Viśvayoni) and he who dwells again and again in bodies (Punarvasu).
m.stotra.sh17: He is the younger brother of Indra (Upendra), the dwarf (Vāmana), the towering (Prāṃśu), he whose deeds never fail (Amogha), the pure (Śuci) and the mighty (Ūrjita); he who surpasses Indra (Atīndra), he who draws all together at the dissolution (Saṅgraha), creation itself (Sarga), he who holds his own being steady (Dhṛtātmā), he who appoints all to their work (Niyama) and he who rules all from within (Yama).
m.stotra.sh18: He is the one to be known (Vedya), the knower of all learning (Vaidya), ever in yoga (Sadāyogī), the slayer of the demon warriors (Vīrahā), the lord of knowledge (Mādhava) and sweet as honey (Madhu); he is beyond the senses (Atīndriya), the great wielder of māyā (Mahāmāya), he of great zeal (Mahotsāha) and he of great strength (Mahābala).
m.stotra.sh19: He is of great intellect (Mahābuddhi), of great valour (Mahāvīrya), of great power (Mahāśakti) and of great radiance (Mahādyuti); he whose form cannot be described (Anirdeśyavapu), the glorious (Śrīmān), he whose nature is beyond measure (Ameyātmā) and he who held up the great mountain (Mahādridhṛk).
m.stotra.sh20: He is the great archer (Maheṣvāsa), the upholder of the earth (Mahībhartā), the abode of Śrī (Śrīnivāsa) and the goal of the good (Satāṃ Gatiḥ); the unobstructed (Aniruddha), he who delights the gods (Surānanda), he who recovered the lost earth (Govinda) and the lord of those who know the sacred word (Govidāṃ Patiḥ).
m.stotra.sh21: He is the radiance of the radiant (Marīci), the subduer of the wicked (Damana), the swan (Haṃsa), he of beautiful wings (Suparṇa) and the best of serpents (Bhujagottama); the golden-navelled (Hiraṇyanābha), he of noble tapas (Sutapā), he from whose navel springs the lotus (Padmanābha) and the lord of creatures (Prajāpati).
m.stotra.sh22: He is the deathless (Amṛtyu), the all-seeing (Sarvadṛk), the lion (Siṃha), he who joins beings to the fruits of their deeds (Sandhātā), he in whom that union rests (Sandhimān) and the steady (Sthira); the unborn (Aja), he whom foes cannot withstand (Durmarṣaṇa), the teacher and ruler (Śāstā), he whose nature is renowned (Viśrutātmā) and the slayer of the gods' enemies (Surārihā).
m.stotra.sh23: He is the teacher (Guru), the greatest of teachers (Gurutama), the supreme abode (Dhāma), the true (Satya) and he of true valour (Satyaparākrama); he whose eyes are closed in yogic sleep (Nimiṣa), the ever-wakeful (Animiṣa), the garlanded (Sragvī), the lord of speech (Vācaspati) and he of noble intellect (Udāradhī).
m.stotra.sh24: He is the one who leads onward to the highest (Agraṇī), the leader of all beings (Grāmaṇī), the glorious (Śrīmān), justice itself (Nyāya), the guide (Netā) and he who moves all as the breath of life (Samīraṇa); the thousand-headed (Sahasramūrdhā), the Self of the universe (Viśvātmā), the thousand-eyed (Sahasrākṣa) and the thousand-footed (Sahasrapāt).
m.stotra.sh25: He is the one who turns the wheel of worldly existence (Āvartana), he whose self is withdrawn from worldly ties (Nivṛttātmā), the one hidden from beings by the veil of ignorance (Saṃvṛta) and the crusher of the wicked (Sampramardana); the sun who brings round the days (Ahaḥ Saṃvartakaḥ), fire (Vahni), the wind (Anila) and the bearer of the earth (Dharaṇīdhara).
m.stotra.sh26: He is the most gracious (Suprasāda), he of serene self (Prasannātmā), the upholder of the universe (Viśvadhṛk), its sustainer (Viśvabhuk) and the all-pervading (Vibhu); he who honours the good (Satkartā), he who is honoured by all (Satkṛta), the righteous (Sādhu), he who draws all beings into himself at the dissolution (Jahnu), the refuge of all beings and of the waters (Nārāyaṇa) and the leader (Nara).
m.stotra.sh27: He is the one whose names and forms cannot be counted (Asaṅkhyeya), he whose nature is beyond measure (Aprameyātmā), the most excellent (Viśiṣṭa), he who lays down the law and protects the good (Śiṣṭakṛt) and the pure (Śuci); he whose every aim is accomplished (Siddhārtha), he whose resolves always come true (Siddhasaṅkalpa), the giver of success (Siddhida) and the means of success (Siddhisādhana).
m.stotra.sh28: He is the one whose day is dharma, the sacrifice (Vṛṣāhī), he who showers blessings on devotees (Vṛṣabha), the all-pervading (Viṣṇu), he to whom the steps are dharma (Vṛṣaparvā) and he in whose womb is dharma (Vṛṣodara); he who makes all grow (Vardhana) and who grows as the world (Vardhamāna), the one apart from all (Vivikta) and the ocean of the Vedas (Śrutisāgara).
m.stotra.sh29: He is of beautiful arms (Subhuja), hard to hold in meditation (Durdhara), the eloquent (Vāgmī), the lord of lords (Mahendra), the giver of wealth (Vasuda) and wealth itself (Vasu); he of many forms (Naikarūpa), of vast form (Bṛhadrūpa), he who pervades the rays (Śipiviṣṭa) and the illuminer (Prakāśana).
m.stotra.sh30: He is the bearer of strength, splendour and radiance (Ojastejodyutidhara), he of luminous nature (Prakāśātmā) and he who gives heat (Pratāpana); the abundant (Ṛddha), he whose syllable Om is clear (Spaṣṭākṣara), the mantra (Mantra), the moon's ray (Candrāṃśu) and he of the sun's brilliance (Bhāskaradyuti).
m.stotra.sh31: He is the one from whom the moon arose (Amṛtāṃśūdbhava), the shining (Bhānu), the moon (Śaśabindu) and the lord of the gods (Sureśvara); the medicine for worldly existence (Auṣadha), the bridge of the world (Jagataḥ Setuḥ) and he whose dharma and valour are true (Satyadharmaparākrama).
m.stotra.sh32: He is the lord of what was, what will be and what is (Bhūtabhavyabhavannātha), the purifying wind (Pavana), he who sets the wind moving and makes pure (Pāvana) and fire (Anala); the destroyer of desire (Kāmahā), the fulfiller of desires (Kāmakṛt), the beautiful (Kānta), the one who is longed for (Kāma), the giver of what is desired (Kāmaprada) and the Lord (Prabhu).
m.stotra.sh33: He is the one who began the ages (Yugādikṛt), he who turns the ages round (Yugāvarta), he of many māyās (Naikamāya) and the great eater who consumes all at the end (Mahāśana); he is the invisible (Adṛśya) and also of manifest form (Vyaktarūpa), the conqueror of thousands (Sahasrajit) and he of endless victory (Anantajit).
m.stotra.sh34: He is the one worshipped in sacrifice (Iṣṭa), the undistinguished, the same in all (Aviśiṣṭa), the one dear to the good (Śiṣṭeṣṭa), the wearer of the peacock feather (Śikhaṇḍī), he who binds all by māyā (Nahuṣa) and dharma itself (Vṛṣa); the destroyer of anger (Krodhahā), he who turns his wrath on the wicked (Krodhakṛt), the doer of all (Kartā), he whose arms are everywhere (Viśvabāhu) and the bearer of the earth (Mahīdhara).
m.stotra.sh35: He is the one who never falls from his nature (Acyuta), the renowned (Prathita), life (Prāṇa), the giver of life (Prāṇada) and the younger brother of Indra (Vāsavānuja); the treasury of the waters (Apāṃnidhi), the ground of all (Adhiṣṭhāna), the ever-vigilant (Apramatta) and he who is established in his own glory (Pratiṣṭhita).
m.stotra.sh36: He is the one who flows forth as nectar (Skanda), the upholder of the path of dharma (Skandadhara), the bearer of the world's burden (Dhurya), the giver of boons (Varada) and he who sets the winds moving (Vāyuvāhana); he is the god who dwells in all (Vāsudeva), he of vast rays (Bṛhadbhānu), the first god (Ādideva) and the destroyer of the strongholds of the gods' enemies (Purandara).
m.stotra.sh37: He is the sorrowless (Aśoka), the one who carries beings across the ocean of worldly existence (Tāraṇa), the saviour (Tāra), the valiant (Śūra), he who was born in the line of Śūra (Śauri) and the lord of all beings (Janeśvara); he is the one favourable to all (Anukūla), he who comes in hundreds of incarnations (Śatāvarta), the bearer of the lotus (Padmī) and he whose eyes are like lotuses (Padmanibhekṣaṇa).
m.stotra.sh38: He is the lotus-navelled (Padmanābha), the lotus-eyed (Aravindākṣa), he who is worshipped within the lotus of the heart (Padmagarbha) and the sustainer of all bodies (Śarīrabhṛt); he is the one of great prosperity (Maharddhi), the abounding (Ṛddha), the ancient self (Vṛddhātmā), the large-eyed (Mahākṣa) and he who bears Garuḍa on his banner (Garuḍadhvaja).
m.stotra.sh39: He is the incomparable (Atula), he who shines in perishable bodies as their inner self (Śarabha), the formidable (Bhīma), he who knows the time for creation, preservation and dissolution (Samayajña) and Hari who receives the oblation (Havirhari); he is the one known through every means of knowledge (Sarvalakṣaṇalakṣaṇya), he who is ever united with Lakṣmī (Lakṣmīvān) and the victor in battle (Samitiñjaya).
m.stotra.sh40: He is the imperishable (Vikṣara), the red-hued (Rohita), the path to the highest state (Mārga), the cause of the world (Hetu), he who was bound with a cord round his waist (Dāmodara) and the one who bears all (Saha); he is the bearer of the earth (Mahīdhara), the most fortunate (Mahābhāga), the swift (Vegavān) and he who consumes beyond measure, devouring the world at dissolution (Amitāśana).
m.stotra.sh41: He is the source from which the world arises (Udbhava), he who stirs nature into motion at creation (Kṣobhaṇa), the shining god (Deva), he who holds Śrī within him (Śrīgarbha) and the supreme Lord (Parameśvara); he is the instrument of creation (Karaṇa), its cause (Kāraṇa), the doer (Kartā), the maker of the manifold world (Vikartā), the unfathomable (Gahana) and the one who hides himself by his māyā (Guha).
m.stotra.sh42: He is resolve itself, determinate knowledge (Vyavasāya), the ground of all order (Vyavasthāna), the final resting place of all (Saṃsthāna), the giver of each one's place according to his deeds (Sthānada) and the steadfast (Dhruva); he is of supreme glory (Pararddhi), supremely manifest (Paramaspaṣṭa), content (Tuṣṭa), full (Puṣṭa) and of auspicious glance (Śubhekṣaṇa).
m.stotra.sh43: He is the delight of all (Rāma), the one in whom all comes to rest (Virāma), turned away from sense objects (Virata), the one whom seekers search for (Mārga), the one to whom knowledge leads (Neya), the leader (Naya) and the one who has no leader (Anaya); he is the hero (Vīra), the best of the mighty (Śaktimatāṃ Śreṣṭhaḥ), dharma (Dharma) and the foremost among the knowers of dharma (Dharmaviduttama).
m.stotra.sh44: He is the one whose way is never hindered (Vaikuṇṭha), the Supreme Person (Puruṣa), the life-breath (Prāṇa), the giver of life (Prāṇada), the syllable Om (Praṇava) and the vast (Pṛthu); he is the golden source of creation (Hiraṇyagarbha), the slayer of the enemies of the gods (Śatrughna), the one who pervades all (Vyāpta), the wind (Vāyu) and the one beyond the reach of the senses (Adhokṣaja).
m.stotra.sh45: He is the season, as time (Ṛtu), of auspicious sight (Sudarśana), time itself (Kāla), the one who abides in the highest place (Parameṣṭhī) and the one held on every side by those seeking refuge (Parigraha); he is the fierce (Ugra), the year (Saṃvatsara), the skilful (Dakṣa), the rest of the weary (Viśrāma) and skilled in all things (Viśvadakṣiṇa).
m.stotra.sh46: He is the one in whom the worlds are spread out (Vistāra), the steadfast and immovable (Sthāvarasthāṇu), the ground of true knowledge (Pramāṇa) and the imperishable seed (Bījam Avyayam); he is the one sought by all (Artha), he who has nothing left to seek (Anartha), he who is enveloped in the great sheaths (Mahākośa), he of great bliss (Mahābhoga) and he of great wealth (Mahādhana).
m.stotra.sh47: He is the never-dejected (Anirviṇṇa), the most vast (Sthaviṣṭha), the unborn (Abhū), the sacrificial post of dharma (Dharmayūpa) and the great sacrifice (Mahāmakha); he is the one who turns the wheel of the stars (Nakṣatranemi), the lord of the stars as the moon (Nakṣatrī), the one able in all things (Kṣama), he who remains when all has wasted away at dissolution (Kṣāma) and he who strives to create and sustain (Samīhana).
m.stotra.sh48: He is the sacrifice (Yajña), the one worthy of worship (Ijya) and the most worthy of worship (Mahejya), the rite (Kratu), the long sacrifice (Satra) and the refuge of the good (Satāṃ Gatiḥ); he is the all-seeing (Sarvadarśī), the ever free (Vimuktātmā), the all-knowing (Sarvajña) and the supreme knowledge (Jñānam Uttamam).
m.stotra.sh49: He is of excellent vows (Suvrata), fair-faced (Sumukha), subtle (Sūkṣma), of auspicious sound (Sughoṣa), the giver of happiness (Sukhada) and the friend of all (Suhṛt); he is the captivator of the mind (Manohara), the conqueror of anger (Jitakrodha), the mighty-armed (Vīrabāhu) and he who tears apart the unrighteous (Vidāraṇa).
m.stotra.sh50: He is the one who lulls beings to sleep by his māyā (Svāpana), the independent (Svavaśa), the all-pervading (Vyāpī), he of many forms (Naikātmā) and the doer of many deeds (Naikakarmakṛt); he is the year (Vatsara), loving to his devotees (Vatsala), the keeper of the calves (Vatsī), the one who holds jewels within (Ratnagarbha) and the lord of wealth (Dhaneśvara).
m.stotra.sh51: He is the protector of dharma (Dharmagup), the one who practises dharma (Dharmakṛt), the upholder of dharma (Dharmī), the real (Sat), the unreal (Asat), the perishable (Kṣara) and the imperishable (Akṣara); he is free from the limited knowing of the individual soul (Avijñātā), thousand-rayed (Sahasrāṃśu), the ordainer (Vidhātā) and marked with auspicious signs (Kṛtalakṣaṇa).
m.stotra.sh52: He is the one who stands amid the wheel of rays as the sun (Gabhastinemi), he who is established in sattva (Sattvastha), the lion (Siṃha) and the great lord of beings (Bhūtamaheśvara); he is the first god (Ādideva), the great god (Mahādeva), the lord of the gods (Deveśa) and the teacher of Indra, who sustains the gods (Devabhṛdguru).
m.stotra.sh53: He is the one who lifts beings out of worldly existence (Uttara), the lord of the cows (Gopati), the protector (Goptā), the one reached through knowledge (Jñānagamya) and the ancient (Purātana); he is the sustainer of the elements that make up the body (Śarīrabhūtabhṛt), the enjoyer (Bhoktā), the lord of the monkeys (Kapīndra) and the one who gives abundant gifts at sacrifices (Bhūridakṣiṇa).
m.stotra.sh54: He is the drinker of the soma at sacrifices (Somapa), the one who drinks the nectar of his own bliss (Amṛtapa), the moon (Soma), the conqueror of many (Purujit) and the best among the great (Purusattama); he is the one who disciplines the wicked (Vinaya), the victorious (Jaya), the one true to his word (Satyasandha), he who was born in the Daśārha clan (Dāśārha) and the lord of the Sātvatas (Sātvatāmpati).
m.stotra.sh55: He is the living soul who sustains life (Jīva), the one who teaches discipline (Vinayitā), the witness (Sākṣī), the giver of liberation (Mukunda) and of boundless valour (Amitavikrama); he is the ocean, the treasury of the waters (Ambhonidhi), the infinite self (Anantātmā), the one who lies on the great ocean (Mahodadhiśaya) and the one who brings all beings to their end (Antaka).
m.stotra.sh56: He is unborn (Aja), most worthy of worship (Mahārha), ever established in his own nature (Svābhāvya), the conqueror of his enemies (Jitāmitra) and the one who gladdens those who meditate on him (Pramodana); he is bliss itself (Ānanda), the giver of joy (Nandana), full of every joy (Nanda), the one whose dharma is true (Satyadharmā) and the one who strode the three worlds in three steps (Trivikrama).
m.stotra.sh57: He is the great sage Kapila, the teacher (Maharṣi Kapilācārya), the one who knows the deeds of all beings (Kṛtajña) and the lord of the earth (Medinīpati); he is the one of the three steps (Tripada), the ruler of the gods (Tridaśādhyakṣa), the one of the great horn as the Fish (Mahāśṛṅga) and the one who brings to an end the world he made (Kṛtāntakṛt).
m.stotra.sh58: He is the great Boar (Mahāvarāha), the one who found the lost earth again (Govinda), the one with a splendid army (Suṣeṇa) and the wearer of golden armlets (Kanakāṅgadī); he is the secret one (Guhya), the profound (Gabhīra), the unfathomable (Gahana), the hidden (Gupta) and the bearer of the discus and the mace (Cakragadādhara).
m.stotra.sh59: He is the creator (Vedhā), the one who is himself his own means in all he does (Svāṅga), the unconquered (Ajita), Kṛṣṇa (Kṛṣṇa), the firm (Dṛḍha), the one who draws all into himself at dissolution (Saṅkarṣaṇa) and the one who never falls from his nature (Acyuta); he is Varuṇa (Varuṇa), the son of Varuṇa (Vāruṇa), steadfast like a tree (Vṛkṣa), lotus-eyed (Puṣkarākṣa) and great-minded (Mahāmanā).
m.stotra.sh60: He is the Blessed Lord (Bhagavān), the one who takes away all fortune at dissolution (Bhagahā), the blissful (Ānandī), the wearer of the garland of forest flowers (Vanamālī) and the one whose weapon is the plough (Halāyudha); he is the son of Aditi (Āditya), the light within the sun (Jyotirāditya), the forbearing (Sahiṣṇu) and the best of goals (Gatisattama).
m.stotra.sh61: He has a splendid bow (Sudhanvā), an axe that cuts his foes to pieces (Khaṇḍaparaśu), is terrible to the unrighteous (Dāruṇa) and gives wealth (Draviṇaprada); he touches the heavens (Divaspṛk), sees all (Sarvadṛk), is Vyāsa who divided the Veda (Vyāsa), the lord of speech (Vācaspati) and the one not born of a womb (Ayonija).
m.stotra.sh62: He is praised by the three Sāmans (Trisāmā), the singer of the Sāman (Sāmaga), the Sāman itself (Sāma), liberation (Nirvāṇa), the medicine for the disease of worldly existence (Bheṣaja) and the physician (Bhiṣak); he established renunciation (Saṃnyāsakṛt), is calm (Śama), serene (Śānta), the ground of all (Niṣṭhā), peace (Śānti) and the supreme refuge (Parāyaṇa).
m.stotra.sh63: He is of beautiful form (Śubhāṅga), the giver of peace (Śāntida), the creator (Sraṣṭā), the one who gladdens the earth (Kumuda) and the one who lies in the waters that encircle the earth (Kuvaleśaya); he does good to the cows (Gohita), is the lord of the earth (Gopati), the protector (Goptā), the one whose glance showers every wish (Vṛṣabhākṣa) and the lover of dharma (Vṛṣapriya).
m.stotra.sh64: He never turns back (Anivartī), has turned his mind from sense objects (Nivṛttātmā), draws the world together at dissolution (Saṅkṣeptā), brings welfare (Kṣemakṛt) and is the auspicious (Śiva); he bears the Śrīvatsa mark on his chest (Śrīvatsavakṣā), is the abode of Śrī (Śrīvāsa), the lord of Śrī (Śrīpati) and the best among the glorious (Śrīmatāṃ Vara).
m.stotra.sh65: He is the giver of fortune (Śrīda), the lord of Śrī (Śrīśa), the dwelling of Śrī (Śrīnivāsa), the treasury of fortune (Śrīnidhi) and the one who distributes fortune according to deeds (Śrīvibhāvana); he bears Śrī (Śrīdhara), brings prosperity (Śrīkara), is the highest good (Śreya), the glorious (Śrīmān) and the refuge of the three worlds (Lokatrayāśraya).
m.stotra.sh66: He is of beautiful eyes (Svakṣa), of beautiful limbs (Svaṅga), of a hundredfold bliss (Śatānanda), supreme joy (Nandi) and the lord of the hosts of lights (Jyotirgaṇeśvara); he has mastered his mind (Vijitātmā), is subject to no one in his nature (Avidheyātmā), is of true renown (Satkīrti) and has no doubt left in him (Chinnasaṃśaya).
m.stotra.sh67: He is exalted above all beings (Udīrṇa), has eyes on every side (Sarvataścakṣu), has no lord over him (Anīśa) and is eternal and unchanging (Śāśvatasthira); he lay upon the ground (Bhūśaya), adorns the world (Bhūṣaṇa), is glory itself (Bhūti), free from grief (Viśoka) and the destroyer of grief (Śokanāśana).
m.stotra.sh68: He is radiant (Arciṣmān), worshipped by all (Arcita), the vessel in which all is contained (Kumbha), utterly pure in his self (Viśuddhātmā) and the purifier (Viśodhana); he is the one whom no one can obstruct (Aniruddha), the one who has no rival (Apratiratha), the one of surpassing wealth (Pradyumna) and of boundless valour (Amitavikrama).
m.stotra.sh69: He is the slayer of Kālanemi (Kālaneminihā), the hero (Vīra), born in the line of Śūra (Śauri) and the lord even of the valiant (Śūrajaneśvara); he is the self of the three worlds (Trilokātmā), the lord of the three worlds (Trilokeśa), the one with beautiful hair (Keśava), the slayer of Keśī (Keśihā) and the remover of sin (Hari).
m.stotra.sh70: He is the god whom all desire (Kāmadeva), the protector of desires (Kāmapāla), the one whose every desire is fulfilled (Kāmī), the lovely (Kānta) and the maker of the scriptures (Kṛtāgama); he is the one whose form cannot be described (Anirdeśyavapu), the all-pervader (Viṣṇu), the hero (Vīra), the endless (Ananta) and Arjuna, who won wealth (Dhanañjaya).
m.stotra.sh71: He is the friend of the Veda, of austerity and of the brāhmaṇas (Brahmaṇya), the maker of Brahman (Brahmakṛt), Brahmā (Brahmā), Brahman (Brahma) and the one who increases Brahman (Brahmavivardhana); he is the knower of the Veda (Brahmavid), the brāhmaṇa (Brāhmaṇa), the possessor of Brahman (Brahmī), the one who knows the Veda as his own self (Brahmajña) and the one dear to the brāhmaṇas (Brāhmaṇapriya).
m.stotra.sh72: He is of mighty strides (Mahākrama), of mighty deeds (Mahākarmā), of great splendour (Mahātejā) and the great serpent (Mahoraga); he is the great rite (Mahākratu), the great sacrificer (Mahāyajvā), the great sacrifice (Mahāyajña) and the great oblation (Mahāhavi).
m.stotra.sh73: He is worthy of praise (Stavya), the one who delights in praise (Stavapriya), the hymn itself (Stotra), praise itself (Stuti), the one who praises (Stotā) and fond of battle (Raṇapriya); he is the full (Pūrṇa), the fulfiller of every wish (Pūrayitā), the purifying (Puṇya), of holy fame (Puṇyakīrti) and free from every ill (Anāmaya).
m.stotra.sh74: He is swift as the mind (Manojava), the maker of tīrthas, the founder of sacred learning (Tīrthakara), the one whose seed is gold (Vasuretā) and the giver of wealth (Vasuprada); he is the giver of the highest wealth, liberation (Vasuprada), the son of Vasudeva (Vāsudeva), the one who dwells in all (Vasu), of excellent mind (Vasumanā) and the oblation itself (Havi).
m.stotra.sh75: He is the goal of the good (Sadgati), the one whose deeds are good (Satkṛti), existence itself (Sattā), of true being and glory (Sadbhūti) and the supreme refuge of the good (Satparāyaṇa); he is the one whose army is of heroes (Śūrasena), the best of the Yadus (Yaduśreṣṭha), the abode of the good (Sannivāsa) and the one whose people by the Yamunā are noble (Suyāmuna).
m.stotra.sh76: He is the dwelling of all beings (Bhūtāvāsa), the god who dwells in all and covers all (Vāsudeva), the abode of all life-breaths (Sarvāsunilaya) and the fire (Anala); he is the destroyer of the pride of the unrighteous (Darpahā), the one who gives pride to those on the path of dharma (Darpada), ever exultant in his own bliss (Dṛpta), hard to hold in the mind (Durdhara) and the unconquered (Aparājita).
m.stotra.sh77: He is the one whose form is the universe (Viśvamūrti), of vast form (Mahāmūrti), of radiant form (Dīptamūrti) and without a body born of karma (Amūrtimān); he is of many forms (Anekamūrti), the unmanifest (Avyakta), of a hundred forms (Śatamūrti) and of a hundred faces (Śatānana).
m.stotra.sh78: He is the one (Eka), the many (Naika), the soma sacrifice (Sava), bliss (Ka), the one to be inquired into (Kim), the Absolute from which all arises (Yat), That (Tat) and the unsurpassed state (Padam Anuttamam); he is the friend of the worlds (Lokabandhu), the lord of the worlds (Lokanātha), born in the line of Madhu (Mādhava) and loving towards his devotees (Bhaktavatsala).
m.stotra.sh79: He is golden in colour (Suvarṇavarṇa), golden of limb (Hemāṅga), of excellent limbs (Varāṅga) and the wearer of delightful armlets (Candanāṅgadī); he is the slayer of the (demon) heroes (Vīrahā), unequalled (Viṣama), the void, free of all attributes (Śūnya), free of all wishes (Ghṛtāśīḥ), the unmoving (Acala) and the moving (Cala).
m.stotra.sh80: He is free of pride (Amānī), the one who gives honour to others (Mānada), worthy of honour (Mānya), the master of the worlds (Lokasvāmī) and the upholder of the three worlds (Trilokadhṛk); he is of excellent intellect (Sumedhā), born of sacrifice (Medhaja), blessed (Dhanya), of true, unerring intellect (Satyamedhā) and the upholder of the earth (Dharādhara).
m.stotra.sh81: He is the one who showers radiance as the sun (Tejovṛṣa), the bearer of splendour (Dyutidhara) and the best of all who bear weapons (Sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ Vara); he accepts what his devotees offer (Pragraha), holds all in check (Nigraha), is ever intent on granting his devotees' wishes (Vyagra), is many-horned (Naikaśṛṅga) and is the elder brother of Gada (Gadāgraja).
m.stotra.sh82: He is of four forms (Caturmūrti), four-armed (Caturbāhu), of four manifestations (Caturvyūha) and the goal of the four stages and orders of life (Caturgati); he is fourfold in his self (Caturātmā), the source of the four aims of life (Caturbhāva), the knower of the four Vedas (Caturvedavit) and the one-footed, a single quarter of whom is the whole world (Ekapāt).
m.stotra.sh83: He is the one who turns the wheel of the world (Samāvarta), the one whose self never withdraws from anything (Anivṛttātmā), hard to conquer (Durjaya) and the one whose command none can transgress (Duratikrama); he is hard to attain (Durlabha), hard to know (Durgama), hard to reach (Durga), hard to bring to dwell in the heart (Durāvāsa) and the slayer of wicked foes (Durārihā).
m.stotra.sh84: He is of auspicious limbs (Śubhāṅga), the one who takes the essence of the worlds as a bee takes honey (Lokasāraṅga), the one whose fair thread is the world spread out (Sutantu) and the one who extends that thread (Tantuvardhana); he is the one whose deeds are like Indra's (Indrakarmā), of mighty deeds (Mahākarmā), the one who has done all there is to do (Kṛtakarmā) and the maker of the scriptures (Kṛtāgama).
m.stotra.sh85: He is the source of all (Udbhava), the beautiful (Sundara), the tender-hearted (Sunda), the one whose navel is lovely as a jewel (Ratnanābha) and of beautiful eyes (Sulocana); he is the sun (Arka), the giver of food (Vājasana), the horned one, as the Fish (Śṛṅgī), the victorious (Jayanta) and the all-knowing conqueror (Sarvavijjayī).
m.stotra.sh86: He is golden of limb (Suvarṇabindu), the unshakeable (Akṣobhya) and the lord even of all the lords of speech (Sarvavāgīśvareśvara); he is the great lake of bliss (Mahāhrada), the great abyss (Mahāgarta), the great being (Mahābhūta) and the great treasure-house (Mahānidhi).
m.stotra.sh87: He is the one who gladdens the earth (Kumuda), the one who gives fruits pure as the kunda flower (Kundara), fair as the kunda jasmine (Kunda), the rain-cloud that rains every wish (Parjanya), the purifier (Pāvana) and the wind (Anila); he is the one whose food is nectar (Amṛtāśa), the one whose body is immortal (Amṛtavapu), the all-knowing (Sarvajña) and the one whose faces are on every side (Sarvatomukha).
m.stotra.sh88: He is easily reached by devotion (Sulabha), of excellent vows (Suvrata), the perfect (Siddha), the conqueror of foes (Śatrujit) and the scorcher of foes (Śatrutāpana); he is the banyan (Nyagrodha), the cluster fig (Udumbara), the pipal (Aśvattha) and the slayer of Cāṇūra the Andhra (Cāṇūrāndhraniṣūdana).
m.stotra.sh89: He is thousand-rayed (Sahasrārci), seven-tongued (Saptajihva), of seven flames (Saptaidhā) and the one whose vehicle is seven horses (Saptavāhana); he is formless (Amūrti), sinless (Anagha), beyond thought (Acintya), the one who brings fear to the wicked (Bhayakṛt) and the destroyer of fear for his devotees (Bhayanāśana).
m.stotra.sh90: He is subtle as an atom (Aṇu), vast (Bṛhat), slender (Kṛśa), massive (Sthūla), the bearer of the guṇas (Guṇabhṛt), beyond the guṇas (Nirguṇa) and the great (Mahān); he is upheld by none (Adhṛta), upheld by himself (Svadhṛta), of lovely face (Svāsya), the one whose line is the first of all (Prāgvaṃśa) and the one who increases the line (Vaṃśavardhana).
m.stotra.sh91: He is the bearer of the burden of the earth (Bhārabhṛt), the one declared in the Vedas as the Supreme (Kathita), the yogī (Yogī), the lord of yogīs (Yogīśa) and the one who grants every wish (Sarvakāmada); he is the resting place of those who wander in the world (Āśrama), the ascetic (Śramaṇa), the one who remains when all has wasted away at the dissolution (Kṣāma), the tree of the world with its fair leaves (Suparṇa) and the one who sets the wind moving (Vāyuvāhana).
m.stotra.sh92: He is the bearer of the bow (Dhanurdhara), the knower of the science of archery (Dhanurveda), the rod of punishment (Daṇḍa), the subduer (Damayitā) and the restraint it brings (Dama); he is the unconquered (Aparājita), the all-enduring (Sarvasaha), the controller (Niyantā), controlled by none (Aniyama) and beyond the reach of death (Ayama).
m.stotra.sh93: He is full of strength and valour (Sattvavān), established in sattva (Sāttvika), the true (Satya) and devoted to truth and dharma (Satyadharmaparāyaṇa); he is the one sought by all who seek the aims of life (Abhiprāya), worthy of the dearest offerings (Priyārha), worthy of worship (Arha), the one who does what is dear to his devotees (Priyakṛt) and the one who increases their love (Prītivardhana).
m.stotra.sh94: He is the one whose path is the sky (Vihāyasagati), the light (Jyoti), of lovely radiance (Suruci), the eater of oblations (Hutabhuk) and the all-pervading (Vibhu); he is the sun that draws up the waters (Ravi), the one who shines in many ways (Virocana), the sun (Sūrya), the begetter of all (Savitā) and the one whose eye is the sun (Ravilocana).
m.stotra.sh95: He is endless (Ananta), the eater of oblations (Hutabhuk), the enjoyer (Bhoktā), the giver of happiness (Sukhada), born many times in his descents (Naikaja) and the first-born (Agraja); he is never dejected (Anirviṇṇa), ever forbearing (Sadāmarṣī), the ground of the worlds (Lokādhiṣṭhāna) and the wondrous (Adbhuta).
m.stotra.sh96: He is the everlasting, time itself (Sanāt), the most ancient (Sanātanatama), the sage Kapila (Kapila), the sun (Kapi) and the imperishable (Avyaya); he is the giver of well-being (Svastida), the one who works well-being (Svastikṛt), well-being itself (Svasti), the one who enjoys and guards well-being (Svastibhuk) and skilled in granting well-being (Svastidakṣiṇa).
m.stotra.sh97: He is free of fierceness (Araudra), the wearer of earrings (Kuṇḍalī), the bearer of the discus (Cakrī), the valiant (Vikramī) and the one whose command is mighty (Ūrjitaśāsana); he is beyond words (Śabdātiga), declared by all the words of the Veda (Śabdasaha), the cool one (Śiśira) and the maker of night (Śarvarīkara).
m.stotra.sh98: He is free of cruelty (Akrūra), lovely and gentle (Peśala), skilful (Dakṣa), kindly and upright (Dakṣiṇa) and the best of the forbearing (Kṣamiṇāṃ Vara); he is the wisest of all (Vidvattama), free of fear (Vītabhaya) and the one to hear of whom and sing of whom brings merit (Puṇyaśravaṇakīrtana).
m.stotra.sh99: He is the one who carries beings across the ocean of the world (Uttāraṇa), the destroyer of evil deeds (Duṣkṛtihā), the holy (Puṇya) and the destroyer of evil dreams (Duḥsvapnanāśana); he is the one who ends the many courses of rebirth (Vīrahā), the protector (Rakṣaṇa), the good, present as the saints (Santaḥ), the giver of life (Jīvana) and the one who stands pervading all around (Paryavasthita).
m.stotra.sh100: He is of endless forms (Anantarūpa), of endless glory (Anantaśrī), the one who has conquered anger (Jitamanyu) and the remover of fear (Bhayāpaha); he is the just, who gives each his due (Caturaśra), of unfathomable being (Gabhīrātmā), the one who grants in many ways (Vidiśa), the one who gives his various commands (Vyādiśa) and the one who, as the Veda, points out the fruits of acts (Diśa).
m.stotra.sh101: He is without beginning (Anādi), the ground of all (Bhū), the splendour of the earth (Bhuvo Lakṣmī), the excellent hero (Suvīra) and the wearer of beautiful armlets (Rucirāṅgada); he is the begetter of beings (Janana), the root cause of their birth (Janajanmādi), the formidable (Bhīma) and of formidable valour (Bhīmaparākrama).
m.stotra.sh102: He is the abode of all supports (Ādhāranilaya), the one who has no upholder (Adhātā), the one who blossoms like a flower (Puṣpahāsa) and ever awake (Prajāgara); he is above all (Ūrdhvaga), the one who walks the path of the good (Satpathācāra), the giver of life (Prāṇada), the sacred syllable Om (Praṇava) and the dealer who gives the fruit in return for acts (Paṇa).
m.stotra.sh103: He is consciousness, the measure of all knowing (Pramāṇa), the abode of the life-breaths (Prāṇanilaya), the one who sustains life (Prāṇabhṛt) and the one who keeps beings alive by the breath (Prāṇajīvana); he is the truth (Tattva), the knower of the truth (Tattvavit), the one Self (Ekātmā) and beyond birth, death and old age (Janmamṛtyujarātiga).
m.stotra.sh104: He is the tree of Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ, the three worlds (Bhūrbhuvaḥsvastaru), the one who carries across (Tāra), the begetter of all (Savitā) and the father even of the grandsire Brahmā (Prapitāmaha); he is the sacrifice (Yajña), the lord of sacrifices (Yajñapati), the sacrificer (Yajvā), the one whose limbs are the sacrifice (Yajñāṅga) and the one who carries sacrifices to their fruit (Yajñavāhana).
m.stotra.sh105: He is the upholder of sacrifice (Yajñabhṛt), its maker (Yajñakṛt), the one to whom sacrifice belongs as its principal (Yajñī), its enjoyer (Yajñabhuk) and the one reached through sacrifice (Yajñasādhana); he is the one who brings sacrifice to its fruit (Yajñāntakṛt), the secret of sacrifice (Yajñaguhya), food (Anna) and the eater of food as well (Annāda).
m.stotra.sh106: He is his own source (Ātmayoni), self-born (Svayañjāta), the one who dug the earth as the Boar (Vaikhāna) and the singer of the Sāman chants (Sāmagāyana); he is the son of Devakī (Devakīnandana), the creator (Sraṣṭā), the lord of the earth (Kṣitīśa) and the destroyer of sin (Pāpanāśana).
m.stotra.sh107: He is the bearer of the conch (Śaṅkhabhṛt), the bearer of the sword Nandaka (Nandakī), the bearer of the discus (Cakrī), the wielder of the bow Śārṅga (Śārṅgadhanvā) and the bearer of the mace (Gadādhara); he is the one with the discus in his hand (Rathāṅgapāṇi), the unshakeable (Akṣobhya) and the one who has every kind of weapon (Sarvapraharaṇāyudha). O bearer of every kind of weapon, Om, salutation to you. Thus the thousand names are complete.
m.stotra.sh108: Wearing the forest garland (Vanamālī), bearing the mace (Gadī), the bow Śārṅga (Śārṅgī), the conch (Śaṅkhī), the discus (Cakrī) and the sword Nandaka (Nandakī), may the glorious Nārāyaṇa, Viṣṇu, Vāsudeva protect us on every side. May Śrī Vāsudeva protect us on every side; Om, salutation to him. Thus the prayer is complete.
m.uttara.sh1: Bhīṣma said: Thus the thousand divine names of the great-souled Keśava, who is worthy of praise, have been recounted in full.
m.uttara.sh2: Whoever hears this daily, and whoever recites it too, that man meets with no ill at all, in the next world or here.
m.uttara.sh3: A brāhmaṇa becomes a master of the Veda, a kṣatriya becomes victorious, a vaiśya grows rich in wealth, and a śūdra gains happiness.
m.uttara.sh4: One who seeks dharma gains dharma, and one who seeks wealth gains wealth; one who desires gains his desires, and one who longs for children gains children.
m.uttara.sh5: The devotee who, always on rising, pure and with his mind set on him, recites these thousand names of Vāsudeva
m.uttara.sh6: gains great fame and pre-eminence among his kin as well; he gains lasting fortune, and he gains the highest good.
m.uttara.sh7: He meets fear nowhere, and he gains valour and radiance; he becomes free from disease, radiant, and endowed with strength, beauty and virtues.
m.uttara.sh8: One afflicted by disease is freed from disease, one who is bound is freed from bondage; one who is afraid is freed from fear, and one in distress is freed from calamity.
m.uttara.sh9: The man who, filled with devotion, praises Puruṣottama daily with the thousand names quickly crosses beyond all difficulties.
m.uttara.sh10: The mortal who takes refuge in Vāsudeva and is wholly devoted to Vāsudeva, his self cleansed of all sins, reaches the eternal Brahman.
m.uttara.sh11: For the devotees of Vāsudeva there is no ill anywhere; the fear of birth, death, old age and disease never arises for them.
m.uttara.sh12: One who recites this hymn, filled with faith and devotion, is blessed with happiness of the self, forbearance, fortune, steadfastness, memory and fame.
m.uttara.sh13: Neither anger nor envy, neither greed nor evil thought arises in those who have done good and are devoted to Puruṣottama.
m.uttara.sh14: Heaven with the moon, the sun and the stars, the sky, the directions, the earth and the great ocean are upheld by the power of the great-souled Vāsudeva.
m.uttara.sh15: This whole world, with its gods, asuras and gandharvas, with its yakṣas, serpents and demons, with all that moves and does not move, is under the sway of Kṛṣṇa.
m.uttara.sh16: The senses, the mind, the intellect, sattva, radiance, strength and steadfastness — these, they say, are Vāsudeva himself, and so too the field (the body) and the knower of the field (the self).
m.uttara.sh17: Of all the scriptures, right conduct is held to come first; dharma springs from right conduct, and the lord of dharma is Acyuta.
m.uttara.sh18: The seers, the ancestors, the gods, the great elements, the dhātus, and this world of moving and unmoving things have all come forth from Nārāyaṇa.
m.uttara.sh19: Yoga, knowledge and Sāṅkhya, the branches of learning, the crafts and other work, the Vedas, the śāstras and realised knowledge — all this comes from Janārdana.
m.uttara.sh20: The one Viṣṇu is the great being, and the many separate beings in their many kinds; pervading the three worlds, he, the self of all beings, enjoys them — the imperishable enjoyer of the universe.
m.uttara.sh21: Let the man who wishes to gain the highest good and happiness recite this hymn to the Lord Viṣṇu, sung by Vyāsa.
m.uttara.sh22: Those who worship the lotus-eyed God — the lord of the universe, the unborn, the imperishable master of the world — never meet defeat. They never meet defeat. Om, salutation.
m.uttara.sh23: Arjuna said: O you whose large eyes are like lotus petals, Padmanābha, best of the gods, be the protector of the devotees who love you, Janārdana.
m.uttara.sh24: The Lord said: Pāṇḍava, whoever wishes to praise me with the thousand names — by him I am praised indeed with a single śloka; of this there is no doubt. I am praised indeed; there is no doubt. Om, salutation.
m.uttara.sh25: Vyāsa said: By Vāsudeva's dwelling in them the three worlds are pervaded; you are the dwelling of all beings: Vāsudeva, salutation to you. Śrī Vāsudeva, salutation to you. Om, salutation.
m.uttara.sh26: Pārvatī said: By what easy means do the learned recite Viṣṇu's thousand names daily? I wish to hear it, my Lord.
m.uttara.sh27: Śiva said: Saying “Śrī Rāma, Rāma, Rāma”, I delight in Rāma, who delights the heart; the name of Rāma, fair-faced one, is equal to those thousand names. The name of Śrī Rāma, fair-faced one. Om, salutation.
m.uttara.sh28: Brahmā said: Salutation to the Infinite, of a thousand forms, of a thousand feet, eyes, heads, thighs and arms; to the eternal Person of a thousand names, who upholds a thousand crore ages, salutation. To him who upholds a thousand crore ages, salutation. Om, salutation.
m.uttara.sh29: Sañjaya said: Where Kṛṣṇa, the lord of yoga, is, and where Pārtha (Arjuna), the archer, is, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and steadfast sound policy: this is my conviction.
m.uttara.sh30: The Lord said: Those people who think of me with no other thought and worship me — for them, ever devoted to me, I bring yogakṣema (gaining what they lack and keeping what they have).
m.uttara.sh31: To protect the good, to destroy the evil-doers, and to establish dharma firmly, I come into being age after age.
m.uttara.sh32: May the afflicted, the despondent, the weak, the frightened, and those caught in terrible diseases, by merely chanting the word “Nārāyaṇa”, be freed from sorrow and become happy.
m.uttara.sh33: Whatever I do with body, speech or mind, or with the senses, with the intellect or the self, or from the bent of my nature, all of it I offer, saying: to Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme.
m.iti: Thus ends the hymn of the divine thousand names of Śrī Viṣṇu. Om tat sat (Om, That is the Real).
m.upasamhara.sh1: Om. I bow again and again to Śrī Rāma, who takes away calamities, gives every kind of wealth, and is the delight of the world. I bow to that Rāmacandra, who destroys the pain of the afflicted and the fear of the frightened, and is the rod of Death to his enemies.
m.upasamhara.sh2: Salutation to Rāma, the bow Kodaṇḍa in his hand and an arrow fitted to the string, who cut down all the demons and wards off calamity.
m.upasamhara.sh3: Salutation to Rāma, to Rāmabhadra, to Rāmacandra, to the Creator, to the Lord of the Raghus, to the Lord, to the husband of Sītā.
m.upasamhara.sh4: In front, behind and at the sides, may the mighty Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, their bows drawn full to the ear, protect me.
m.upasamhara.sh5: Ready for battle, in armour, sword at his side, bearing bow and arrows, youthful, may Rāma, with Lakṣmaṇa, always going before me, protect me.
m.upasamhara.sh6: By the medicine of uttering the names Acyuta, Ananta and Govinda, all diseases perish: I say this truly, truly.
m.upasamhara.sh7: Truly, truly, and again truly, it is said with arm raised: there is no scripture higher than the Veda, and no god higher than Keśava.
m.upasamhara.sh8: When the body is worn out and seized by disease, the medicine is the water of the Gaṅgā, and the physician is Nārāyaṇa, Hari.
m.upasamhara.sh9: Having searched through all the scriptures and reflected again and again, this one thing stands well established: Nārāyaṇa, Hari, is the one to meditate on.
m.upasamhara.sh10: Whatever has slipped in a syllable or a word, and whatever falls short of a mātrā (a vowel's measure), may all that be forgiven, O God; Nārāyaṇa, salutation to you.
m.upasamhara.sh11: Visargas, bindus and mātrās, words, quarter-verses and syllables, whether too few or too many, forgive them, Puruṣottama.
m.paryaya.sh1: Salutation to Kamalanābha, with the lotus at his navel; salutation to you who lie on the waters; salutation to you, Keśava, Ananta; Vāsudeva, salutation to you.
m.paryaya.sh2: Salutation to the God who cherishes the Veda and the brāhmaṇas, and to him who works the good of cows and brāhmaṇas; to Kṛṣṇa, who works the good of the world, to Govinda, salutation again and again.
m.paryaya.sh3: As water fallen from the sky goes to the ocean, so a salutation to any of the gods goes to Keśava.
m.paryaya.sh4: This is the path free of thorns, where Hari is worshipped; a teaching without Govinda should be known as a wrong path.
m.paryaya.sh5: Whatever merit lies in all the Vedas and whatever fruit in all the holy places, that fruit one gains in full by praising the God Janārdana.
m.paryaya.sh6: The man who recites it daily in a temple of Keśava, at the three times of day, or twice, or once, drives away every cruel harm.
m.paryaya.sh7: His enemies are burnt up, all the planets are ever gentle to him, and sins melt away, when this hymn is recited.
m.paryaya.sh8: By whom this hymn is meditated on, by whom it is heard, by whom it is recited — by him all gifts have been given and all the gods duly worshipped.
m.paryaya.sh9: In this world or the next there is no fear anywhere for one who recites the thousand names on dvādaśī, the twelfth day of the lunar fortnight, in my (the Lord's) presence.
m.paryaya.sh10: Those who recite it burn away, little by little, sins even of hundreds of crores of kalpas. Pārtha, near the aśvattha tree, meditating on Keśava in the mind,
m.paryaya.sh11: one who recites the thousand names gains the fruit of giving a crore of cows. One who recites it daily in a temple of Śiva, seated in a grove of tulasī,
m.paryaya.sh12: gains liberation: such is the word of the discus-bearer (Viṣṇu). Every sin, the grave killing of a brāhmaṇa and the rest, perishes.
m.paryaya.sh13: Sins dissolve away — what then of other sins? Freed from all sins, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu.
